speaker: Ben Bloom, CEO, Atom Computing
verdict_reasoning:
Evidence gathered from the pre-registered resolver sources only. The criteria required a commercial customer to have RECEIVED AND OPERATED a system matching the 24-entangled-logical-qubit specification by 31 Dec 2025 plus the 30-day grace (30 Jan 2026), and said in advance that an order or a demo does not count.

One commercial sale is identifiable in the named sources: QuNorth (Denmark, funded by EIFO and the Novo Nordisk Foundation), which contracted in 2025 for Magne — an Atom Computing / Microsoft system specified at roughly 50 logical qubits on about 1,225 physical neutral atoms, announced July 2025 with construction beginning that autumn. As of 2 September 2026, more than seven months after the grace period closed, The Quantum Insider reports that the building intended to house Magne has only just been completed, that installation is beginning, and that the system is expected to be fully operational in spring 2027.

So no system was operating at a customer site inside the window — not at the announced 24-logical specification, and not at the differently-specified 50-logical one. That also rules out PARTIALLY_VERIFIED, which required a differently-specified system to have shipped in the window; none did. The January 2025 HPCwire roll-out report logged at intake describes an offering being made available, not a delivery — exactly the distinction the criteria fixed in advance, which is the whole reason it was fixed in advance.

Nothing here is a judgement about intent. Hardware schedules slip, and the original announcement was explicit that delivery was a 2025 plan. What the Ledger records is that the dated, falsifiable version of the claim did not come true inside its own window.

checkins.note: A January 2025 report describes an on-premise system from the same Atom Computing/Microsoft partnership supporting up to 50 logical qubits -- more than this claim's own 24, which is why this is logged on_track rather than off_track. Not treated as a resolution: the desk still needs to confirm this is the SAME delivery the original claim described, not a different, larger, later system being counted as satisfying an earlier, smaller promise.

Flagged resolvable by the seeding pass, NOT resolved -- a January 2025 follow-up report (HPCwire) described Atom Computing and Microsoft rolling out an on-premise system supporting up to 50 logical qubits, which reads as meeting or exceeding this claim, but the desk should verify the exact 24-logical-qubit specification was what actually shipped before writing a VERIFIED verdict, per the two-key rule.
verbatim: By coupling our state-of-the-art neutral-atom qubits with Microsoft's qubit-virtualization system, we are now able to offer reliable logical qubits on a commercial quantum machine.
headline: Atom Computing and Microsoft announced a commercial quantum machine with 24 entangled logical qubits, available for delivery in 2025.
resolution_criteria: Resolves VERIFIED if a commercial customer actually received and operated a system matching the 24-entangled-logical-qubit specification by 31 Dec 2025 (plus grace) -- an order or a demo does not count, an operating delivered system does. PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if a related but differently-specified system shipped in the window (e.g. a different logical-qubit count) instead of the exact one announced. NOT_VERIFIED if no delivery happened in the stated window at all.
